findings.issue: `buildMarketFeedbackInputFromCalculation` silently dropped the `MarketStatus: result.MarketStatus,` field assignment when building `service.MarketFeedbackCalculationInput` from a `CalculationResult`. This line is present at HEAD (commit 1fa9574) and is gone in the working tree, with no mention anywhere in the task spec, the two self-disclosed deviations, or any comment in the diff. It is unrelated to Task 6's stated scope (owner resolution / index shifting).
findings.impact: `MarketFeedbackCalculationInput.MarketStatus` (internal/service/deepseek.go:41) is read directly by `formatCalculationForPrompt` (internal/service/deepseek.go:523-540), which renders the line `Статус относительно рынка по внутренней логике: %s` into the DeepSeek prompt via `emptyOrUnknown(item.MarketStatus)`. With the field never populated, every 'masterpiece'-mode calculate call that triggers the embedded AI feedback (`handleCalculate`, http.go, `h.deepseek != nil && result.CalculationMode == "masterpiece"` branch) now silently sends 'не указано' (not specified) instead of the actual computed market status (e.g. in_market/below_market/above_market from `detectMarketStatus`, costing.go:862). This degrades AI feedback quality for every masterpiece calculation, in production, with zero errors, zero logs, and zero test failures — go build and go test both pass. No handler test exercises `buildMarketFeedbackInputFromCalculation` or asserts on `MarketFeedbackCalculationInput.MarketStatus`, so this regression has no safety net at all.
findings.recommendation: Restore `MarketStatus: result.MarketStatus,` in the `MarketFeedbackCalculationInput{...}` composite literal inside `buildMarketFeedbackInputFromCalculation` (http.go, in the `Calculation: &service.MarketFeedbackCalculationInput{...}` block). Add a handler-level test asserting the DeepSeek input built from a `CalculationResult` carries `MarketStatus` through unchanged, so a future edit in this area can't silently drop it again.

findings.issue: There is no repository-contract test suite for chat-scoped operations (`DeleteChat`, `RestoreChat`, `CreateChat`, `ListChats`, `AppendCalculation`) that runs identically against both `MemoryRepository` and `PostgresRepository`, mirroring what Task 3's `access_repo_test.go` does for the access/user-row methods (`EnsureUser`, `GetUser`, `SetAccess`, etc.). Confirmed by grep: only `access_repo_test.go` and `service/access_test.go` reference `MemoryRepository`/`PostgresRepository` together; no `*_test.go` under `internal/repository` exercises chat methods against both backends.
findings.impact: This is exactly the vulnerability class Task 6 closes (IDOR via owner-scoping). The implementer's own report notes a mutation that broke owner-scoping in `MemoryRepository.DeleteChat` was caught only by the new handler-level test in `http_test.go` (`TestHandleUsers_ForeignOwnerUnreachable`'s 'идентификатор чужого чата на удалении' subtest), not by any repository-level contract test. `PostgresRepository.DeleteChat` (internal/repository/postgres.go:339) currently does scope correctly (`WHERE user_id = ? AND id = ?`), so there is no live bug today — but the only thing standing between a future regression there and a shipped IDOR is a handler test that happens to construct its fixtures against `MemoryRepository`, not `PostgresRepository` (see access_test.go's routeFixture, which always wires `repository.NewMemoryRepository()`). A broken WHERE clause in the Postgres implementation specifically would ship silently: it's never exercised by the handler test suite (which needs DB-less fixtures) and never exercised by a repo contract test (which doesn't exist for chats).
findings.recommendation: Out of Task 6's formal scope (this is Task 3's `costing`/chat repository surface), but flag for a follow-up task: add a chat-repository contract suite parallel to access_repo_test.go that runs `DeleteChat`/`RestoreChat`/`CreateChat`/`ListChats`/`AppendCalculation` against both `MemoryRepository` and a real `PostgresRepository` (behind `TEST_DB_DSN`, same pattern as access_repo_test.go's `TestMain`), asserting owner-scoping explicitly (a delete/restore/list by user A must never observe or mutate user B's rows even when chat IDs collide).

findings.issue: `AccessHandler.identity(w, r)` is now a pure one-line forwarder to the package-level `requireIdentity(w, r)` — it does nothing but rename the call. Meanwhile `APIHandler.handleUsers` in http.go calls `requireIdentity(w, r)` directly, with no equivalent receiver-method wrapper. The two handlers in the same package now use two different calling conventions for the identical operation (`h.identity(w, r)` vs `requireIdentity(w, r)`), which is a needless inconsistency introduced by this diff (access.go used to have its own real implementation, now it's a trivial pass-through kept only for call-site compatibility).
findings.impact: Not a functional bug — both paths resolve to the same fail-closed logic. But a reader hitting `h.identity(w, r)` in access.go has to jump to middleware.go to discover it's just `requireIdentity` under another name, for no behavioral reason. It slightly undercuts the stated goal of the extraction ('one copy of the rule') by leaving a second name for the same one copy.
findings.recommendation: Pick one convention: either delete `AccessHandler.identity` and update its four call sites (handleMe, handleCreateRequest, handleListUsers, handleSetAccess) to call `requireIdentity(w, r)` directly like http.go does, or keep the wrapper but say explicitly in its doc comment that it exists solely to avoid touching four call sites in this diff (a real reason, but distinct from 'the rule lives in one place' framing currently used).

summary: Two major findings and one minor. The core Task 6 change — index-shift across all nine route shapes, owner sourced from requireIdentity/context instead of the URL, the requireIdentity extraction, and the openapi.yaml updates — is correct and verified by hand: every len(parts)/parts[index] pair in the new switch matches the old one shifted down by exactly one, the 404 fallback for the legacy {userID} segment is preserved, and openapi.yaml's five rewritten paths plus four new access/admin paths match the actual route table, JSON tags (UserRecord, AccessState), and the exact set of session-rejection codes emitted by RequireAuth/RequireSameOrigin. go build and go test ./... both pass. However, the diff also silently deletes an unrelated struct field assignment (MarketStatus) in buildMarketFeedbackInputFromCalculation, which is a real, untested, undisclosed functional regression to the DeepSeek market-feedback prompt for masterpiece-mode calculations — this must be restored before merge. Separately, the implementer's self-flagged repository test gap around owner-scoping (DeleteChat and friends) is real and worth a follow-up task given it's precisely the bug class this feature closes, even though it's Task 3's scope. A minor style inconsistency in the requireIdentity extraction (AccessHandler wraps it, APIHandler doesn't) rounds out the findings.
